articles.title: Tesla EVs get a plug-and-charge option at IONNA through the Presto app
articles.summary: IONNA and Presto Charging now let a compatible Tesla start a session at IONNA fast chargers by plugging in, after a one-time setup in the Presto app. That is useful for drivers who cannot charge at home, though some cars from before 2022 may not work, and the first Autocharge session is the one Presto says will be free.

articles.title: Latest Canadian budget packs funding for 55,000 new EV chargers
articles.summary: Canada's proposed budget renews the Zero-Emission Vehicle Infrastructure Program with about $587 million CAD, inside a larger plan for more than 55,000 chargers. Charging-industry groups say the money has to reach condo and apartment buildings, not only highway fast chargers, because those residents still have the hardest time plugging in where they park.

articles.title: Lamppost EV chargers proposed for 26 Leigh and Milton streets
articles.summary: Southend is asking residents until November 18 about 26 lamppost chargers in Leigh and Milton, most of them next to a bay that only an electric car could use while it is charging. The rollout is aimed at drivers with no off-street parking, and a gas car would lose that space for an 18-month trial.

articles.title: Mercedes' EV charging network hit 100 locations after 3 years in the U.S.
articles.summary: Mercedes-Benz High-Power Charging now has 100 sites and nearly 1,000 ports in the U.S. and British Columbia, and only about 7 percent of locations are still CCS-only. Sessions that start on the first try are above 90 percent, and posted prices run about $0.35 to $0.60 per kWh, which is the rate drivers pay when they cannot charge at home.

articles.title: EV chargers in flats: the right to plug, country by country
articles.summary: In much of the EU, an apartment owner or tenant can now install a charger on their own parking space with notice rather than a vote of the other owners, after member states were due to transpose the buildings directive by May 2026. England still has no such right, so a leaseholder needs the freeholder's consent, and a consultation on an "ability to charge" stays open until December 16.

articles.title: ESB increasing its public EV charging rates again
articles.summary: Ireland's largest public charging network raised prices again on November 2, citing wholesale electricity costs, the second increase this year. Pay-as-you-go app rates are now 70 cents per kWh on standard chargers and 83 cents on fast chargers, so drivers who cannot charge at home pay the full increase unless they switch to an off-peak subscription.
